attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses this assessment in his own words.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the scope, conflicting reasons and qualification about his information. That qualification does not make the asserted current state probabilistic.

contract.note: Reading almost everyone as near-universal dissatisfaction among relevant stakeholders is ordinary and fair. The contract appropriately distinguishes that assertion from selected criticism. Its statement that publication time is unavailable conflicts with the supplied timestamp, but does not determine this result.

evidence.note: Documents criticism of the advance draft before the target date. It does not establish stakeholder satisfaction on February 10.
Documents conflicting regulatory preferences and concerns about AI. These do not establish conflicting complaints about the summit or the proportion dissatisfied with it.

Google's prepared remarks provide a favorable participant assessment, weighing against the characterization. This company disclosure is not an independent finding or representative measure; its timing relative to Marcus's post is uncertain.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes selected advance criticism, divergent policy preferences and one favorable participant reaction. It supplies no representative evidence establishing either near-universal dissatisfaction or substantial satisfaction across constituencies on February 10. Neither resolution condition is met.
